STEP 1 - Scene: A small pile of dark, oval, wrinkled fruits, looks like dried dates or prunes (or possibly raisins/olives), on a white plate. Not a full meal; only a small snack portion.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White square-ish plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area = 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Dark dried fruit pieces (about 7 pieces), likely prunes/dates.

STEP 4 - Area: The fruit cluster occupies a small corner area, roughly 4 x 5 cm of the plate, about 2.5% of vessel area (~13 cm^2).

STEP 5 - Volume: 13 cm^2 x 1.5 cm height ≈ 20 ml gross.

STEP 6 - Grams: Dried fruit bulk density ~0.7 g/ml → about 14 g. Seven pitted-size prunes/dates at roughly 7-10 g each would be ~50-60 g, so the pile is likely closer to 40-50 g. I'll take the visual evidence of seven fairly large pieces as the better estimate: ~45 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Dried dates/prunes ≈ 280 kcal per 100 g. 45 g x 2.8 = ~126 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Seven dried fruit pieces is a plausible small snack portion; ~45 g and ~125 kcal fits what is visible.
